tweet:
🖤 New Zealand hit back — 5-wicket win over West Indies at Providence.

West Indies were cruising at 63/0 before Jayden Lennox turned into an absolute menace, ripping out a career-best 5/19 to fold them for just 138. John Campbell's 43 was the only thing resembling resistance.

New Zealand's chase wasn't exactly serene either — 96/5 on a pitch spinning like a fairground ride — until Tom Latham (37*) and Mark Bracewell calmly walked them home.

New Zealand won by 5 wickets with 104 balls to spare. Player of the Match: Jayden Lennox. Series tied 1-1 — Providence giving nobody an easy day. 🔥
imageSource: ESPNcricinfo — Jayden Lennox celebrating during his career-best 5/19, West Indies vs New Zealand, 2nd ODI, Providence, 13 Jul 2026 (this match, NZ ODI kit, live action)

tweet:
🇮🇳 India didn't just win at Lord's — they redecorated the honours board.

285 all out, built on Mandhana (83), Harmanpreet (58) & Deepti Sharma (57). Debutant Kranti Gaud then turned the Long Room into a horror movie, ripping through England for 170.

Set an outrageous 457, Yastika Bhatia shrugged and became the first woman in history to score a Test century at Lord's (112) — then kissed the pitch for good measure. England folded for 186.

142 years Lord's waited to host a women's Test. India showed up and won it by 270 runs. New landlords at the Home of Cricket. 🔥
imageSource: France 24 (AFP) — Yastika Bhatia batting for India, England Women vs India Women, inaugural Women's Test, Lord's, 12 Jul 2026 (this match, India Test whites, live action)

tweet:

1-0 down after Axar Patel's all-rounder special at Edgbaston, this is now win-or-the-series-is-gone for the hosts. India smell blood.

Sophia Gardens, Cardiff. 1 PM local. Do-or-die starts now. 🔥

tweet:
Bazball just lost a Test match it can't come back from. 🏴

McCullum's stepped down as England's Test coach — a 4-1 Ashes flogging and a 2-1 home series defeat to New Zealand did what four years of "just enjoy yourselves lads" couldn't survive.

The twist: he keeps the white-ball job, where England are No.1 in the world. Turns out the format with fewer vibes and more discipline is the one still standing.

Four years, one format left. 🔥

tweet:
🇮🇳 Virat Kohli needs FOUR runs today to become India's all-time leading ODI run-scorer in England — overtaking a Rahul Dravid mark that's stood since 2011.

He fell for 5 in the series opener. Rohit's stalking the same list from a bit further back. One nervous single at Cardiff and the record books get rewritten before lunch.

Sophia Gardens, 5:30 PM IST. Four runs from immortality. 🔥

tweet:
🌴 vs 🖤 — Providence again, decider energy a game early.

Series tied 1-1: West Indies banked Keacy Carty's ton in Game 1, New Zealand hit back through Jayden Lennox's wrecking-ball 5/19 in Game 2. Somebody has to blink.

Daryl Mitchell's averaging a frankly rude 111 in his last five ODIs. Shai Hope isn't far behind — 64 across his last ten. Two in-form captains-in-waiting, one ground that's picked no favourites all series.

Providence Stadium, Guyana. 2:30 PM local. Round three, no clear favourite. 🔥

tweet:
🇮🇳 vs 🏴 — Cardiff, and Bumrah's still doing Bumrah things.

India huffed and puffed to 233 all out in 44 overs, hardly a total to lose sleep over. Then Bumrah removed Ben Duckett with the very first ball of the chase, Bethell followed soon after, and Harry Brook tried to scoop his way out of trouble straight into Ishan Kishan's gloves.

England 56/3 in 12, chasing 234. Joe Root's out there alone, playing solitaire while the required rate creeps past 4.7 an over.

1-0 down in the series, and the pitch is doing India's talking for them. 🔥

tweet:
🖤 New Zealand did it again — 6-wicket win over West Indies at Providence, and at this point Guyana should start charging West Indies rent for hosting the collapse.

Bowled out for 140, done in by spin for the SECOND time this series. Jayden Lennox picked up 4 more, with Bracewell and Santner grabbing 2 apiece, on a pitch where spinners have now taken 22 wickets to the quicks' 6.

New Zealand strolled home in 39.3 overs — 141/4, 63 balls unused, hardly a chase at all.

New Zealand won by 6 wickets. Player of the Match: Jayden Lennox. West Indies now 2-1 down with two to go — déjà vu really isn't a compliment. 🔥

tweet:
🏴 England beat India by 4 wickets in Cardiff — series level 1-1, and Joe Root just played one of the great "so close, yet perfect" innings.

England were in genuine strife: Duckett gone off the first ball to Bumrah, then 125/5 by the 25th over. Root simply refused to get out — 99 not out off 133 balls, calmly cashing in nine boundaries while wickets fell around him like it was a group project he never signed up for.

India's 234 leaned on Kohli (65) and Shreyas Iyer (66), before Archer (3/47) and Atkinson (3/50) turned the tail into scrap metal.

Gus Atkinson finished it with a boundary — sparing Root a lifetime of "what could've been." Player of the Match: Joe Root. 99 not out, basically a hundred with better manners. Series 1-1, Lord's decides it all on Sunday. 🔥
imageSource: ESPNcricinfo — Joe Root pulls one away, England vs India, 2nd ODI, Cardiff, 16 Jul 2026 (this match, England ODI kit, live action)

tweet:
🏏 Sunday's Lord's decider isn't the first time this fixture has turned iconic on that ground.

2002 NatWest final: India were 146/5, chasing an impossible 326. Mohammad Kaif (87*) and Yuvraj Singh (69) somehow got them home with 3 balls to spare — and Sourav Ganguly ripped his shirt off on the balcony to celebrate.

Different decade, same ground, same stakes. India vs England, Lord's, this Sunday. The ghosts of 2002 are watching. 🔥

tweet:

BCCI has officially said this ISN'T his last ODI. His parents flying into London begs to differ. Two 20s in the last two games doesn't help the case either.

Nothing settles a farewell debate like a hundred. Series on the line, Lord's honours board right there — either he goes out arguing with the selectors, or he goes out arguing with physics after clearing the pavilion. 🔥
imageSource: ESPNCricinfo — Rohit Sharma batting, England vs India, 1st ODI, Edgbaston, July 14, 2026 (this series, India ODI kit, live action)

tweet:
🏴 vs 🇮🇳 — Lord's just got a new landlord, and it's Ben Duckett.

England posted 387/3, the highest ODI total in the ground's history, breaking a 47-year-old individual record along the way — Duckett's 141 off 135 balls (18 fours, 1 six) is now the biggest score anyone's ever made at Lord's in a one-dayer.

He didn't do it alone. Jacob Bethell (91 off 93) joined him for a 192-run stand, England's biggest ODI partnership against India ever, beating Root-Morgan's 186 from 2018. Joe Root then strolled in and casually smashed an unbeaten 71 off 48 like it was Tuesday nets.

387 on the board. Series decider. England have said their piece. 🔥
imageSource: France 24 (AFP) — Ben Duckett batting during his century, England vs India, 3rd ODI, Lord's, 19 Jul 2026 (this match, England ODI kit, live action)

tweet:
🌴 vs 🖤 — Bridgetown, and the series is already over. Dignity isn't.

New Zealand sealed it 3-1 with a stomach-churning 1-wicket win — Gudakesh Motie's maiden 5-for (5/47) nearly engineered the great escape before Mitchell Santner's ice-cold 34* dragged the Black Caps home with 35 balls to spare.

West Indies are staring down a grim 4-1 scoreline and a slide toward World Cup qualifiers. New Zealand fancy the clean sweep — Mark Chapman's timing everything right now.

Kensington Oval, Bridgetown. 11 PM IST. Nothing left to win except pride. 🔥
imageSource: ESPNcricinfo — Mark Chapman batting, West Indies vs New Zealand, 4th ODI, Bridgetown, 19 Jul 2026 (this series, New Zealand ODI kit, live action)

tweet:
🏴 vs 🇮🇳 — England win the series 2-1, and India somehow contrived to lose a game where they scored 360.

Duckett (141) and Bethell put on a stand that helped England rack up 387/3 — the highest ODI total Lord's has ever seen — and they still needed every run of it, hanging on by just 27 as India's chase nearly blew the roof off.

Rohit Sharma made sure it wasn't a full humiliation: 138 off the "is-this-his-last-ODI" special, the first Indian man EVER to score a century at Lord's, his 8th ton on English soil. The bowling attack, meanwhile, spent the day cosplaying traffic cones.

England won by 27 runs, series 2-1. Rohit got a standing ovation. Everyone else got a group chat full of question marks. 🔥
imageSource: Livemint (ANI) — Rohit Sharma celebrating his century, England vs India, 3rd ODI, Lord's, 19 Jul 2026 (this match, India ODI kit, live action)

tweet:
🌴 vs 🖤 — West Indies refused to let this series end in embarrassment. Fair play.

New Zealand rocked up in Bridgetown one win from an outright 4-1 sweep. Instead, West Indies bowled first, chased 269, and stumbled over the line at 269/8 with 15 balls to spare — the least convincing "we meant to do that" in recent memory. Shimron Hetmyer, recalled after 13 months away from the ODI side, picked a funny day to remember he's actually good at this.

It capped a series that flipped like a fidget spinner: West Indies won the opener by 7 wickets, New Zealand won the next two, then somehow survived Gudakesh Motie's 5-for to scrape Game 4 by a single wicket.

New Zealand win the series 3-2. West Indies keep their pride; New Zealand keep the trophy and a minor heart condition. 🔥
imageSource: Daily Pioneer — New Zealand batter facing West Indies wicketkeeper, 5th ODI, Kensington Oval, Bridgetown, 21 Jul 2026 (this match, NZ/WI ODI kits, live action)

tweet:
🇮🇳 India just lost an ODI series 2-1 to England — and are still the World No.1 ODI side.

England won the decider at Lord's defending a mammoth 387, and that only got them to 7th in the ICC rankings (93 rating points). India, fresh off that Lord's heartbreak, remain top with 116 — five points clear of New Zealand.

Rankings math is a mood: lose the series, keep the crown. 🔥

18 balls to a maiden T20I fifty against Zimbabwe — 4 fours, 4 sixes, the fastest half-century by a teenager for any full-member nation. Out next ball, because apparently subtlety wasn't in the contract.

🏏 Trivia of the Day

🏴 vs 🇮🇳 — 25 July, and Lord's peaked once before this fixture ever needed reminding.

2011: the 2000th Test match in history, the 100th ever played between these two. Kevin Pietersen marked the occasion with 202* — his only Lord's double hundred — while Rahul Dravid's lone century went to waste as England won by 196 runs.

Round numbers, big stages, one ground that keeps collecting them. 🔥
